description:
Pułtusk Castle stands on a raised mound beside the Narew river, in the Masovian town of the same name. The site belonged to the bishops of Płock from the 12th century, and a surviving document from 1232 already refers to the upkeep of the stronghold here, near a former river ford and the bridge that later replaced it. Sources disagree on the exact dating of the earlier medieval castle, placing it anywhere between the 14th and 16th centuries, so no single construction year is given here.

The castle was rebuilt in Baroque and Classical styles after repeated damage over the centuries, and in the 19th century the Russian authorities confiscated the building and used it as a hospital. Its most severe blow came in 1945, when it burned, and the reconstruction that followed was completed by 1989 — the building was given a new role as Dom Polonii, the World Polonia Centre, named after the pianist and statesman Ignacy Jan Paderewski, serving as a centre for the Polish diaspora.

Little medieval fabric survives today: only the two turrets flanking the entrance by the bridge keep a Gothic form, and even these are largely postwar reconstruction rather than original fabric. The building now operates as a hotel and conference centre.
history: Pułtusk was held by the bishops of Płock from the 12th century, and their castle stood on the Narew near the ford and later bridge. After repeated damage it was rebuilt in Baroque and Classical style; in the 19th century the Russians took it over as a hospital. It burned in 1945 and was rebuilt by 1989 to serve as Dom Polonii, a centre for the Polish diaspora named after Paderewski. Sources disagree on the dating of the earlier castle (14th to 16th century), so no construction year is given here.

faqs.question: Is Pułtusk Castle medieval?
faqs.answer: Only partly in origin. The bishops of Płock held a stronghold here from the Middle Ages, but the present building is a Baroque and Classical rebuild that burned in 1945 and was reconstructed by 1989; only the two entrance turrets keep a Gothic form.

faqs.question: What is Dom Polonii?
faqs.answer: The name given to the castle after its postwar reconstruction, as a centre for the Polish diaspora named after Ignacy Jan Paderewski; today it operates as a hotel and conference centre.
